grade.verdict_quote: Not ready to merge — `go test ./...` passes, but that's because the existing test suite doesn't exercise the edge cases the ticket actually calls out.

D2.quote: Omitting `due` from a PATCH body wipes the task's existing due date (`handlers.go:155` sets `t.Due = due` unconditionally instead of only when present). ... Omitting `tags` wipes existing tags likewise (`t.Tags = req.Tags` unconditionally).
D2.evidence: TestProbe_PatchPreservesUnsetFields → "probe_test.go:39: due wiped by patch: {ID:t0001 Title:y Done:false Due:0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC Tags:[] CreatedAt:2026-03-10 01:00:00 +0000 UTC}" — the printed struct shows both Due reset to zero and Tags:[] (originally ["a","b"])

D3.quote: Migrated tasks lose `CreatedAt` — `migrate.go:42` builds the new `Task` without copying `o.Created`.
D3.evidence: TestProbe_MigratePreservesCreatedAtAndNormalizesLabels → "probe_test.go:95: created_at not preserved: got 0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC want 2025-11-02 08:00:00 +0000 UTC"

D4.quote: v1 labels aren't trimmed/lowercased during migration (`strings.Split(o.Labels, ",")` with no normalization), so `"Health, personal"` becomes tags `"Health"` and `" personal"` instead of `"health"`/`"personal"` as required ("same rules as in create").

D5.quote: A task due *today* is also reported as overdue — the comparison should be `Due.Before(today)`, not "not after."
D5.evidence: TestProbe_OverdueDueToday → "probe_test.go:28: task due today reported overdue: [{ID:t0001 Title:due today Done:false Due:2026-03-10 00:00:00 +0000 UTC ...}]"

D6.quote: Tasks with no due date show up as overdue — `handlers.go:84` compares `t.Due.After(today)`, and a zero-value `Due` is never "after" today, so it slips through.
D6.evidence: TestProbe_OverdueNoDueDate → "probe_test.go:18: task with no due date reported overdue: [{ID:t0001 Title:no due date Done:false Due:0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC ...}]"

D7.quote: Tags sent via PATCH are never trimmed/lowercased/limited — `normalizeTags` isn't called in `patchTask`, so `" Home "` stays as-is and 6+ tags are silently accepted instead of returning 400.
D7.evidence: TestProbe_PatchNormalizesTags → "probe_test.go:53: patch tags not normalized: [ Home   Work ]"; TestProbe_PatchTooManyTagsRejected → "probe_test.go:62: expected 400 for >5 tags on patch, got 200 body={... \"tags\":[\"a\",\"b\",\"c\",\"d\",\"e\",\"f\"] ...}"

D8.quote: Deleting an unknown id returns `204` instead of `404` — `Store.Delete` calls Go's `delete()` on the map, which is a no-op for a missing key and never surfaces `ErrNotFound`.
D8.evidence: TestProbe_DeleteUnknownID → "probe_test.go:71: expected 404 deleting unknown id, got 204"

unsupported_claims.claim: I wrote targeted probe tests ... and found **7 confirmed bugs**, all reproducible
unsupported_claims.why: Bug #7 as stated bundles two behaviours (CreatedAt loss and un-normalized migrated labels). The tool log shows the migration probe test (TestProbe_MigratePreservesCreatedAtAndNormalizesLabels) failing with a Fatalf on the CreatedAt check only ("created_at not preserved: got 0001-01-01... want 2025-11-02..."); because Fatalf halts the test, no output ever demonstrates the claimed resulting tag values ("Health"/" personal"). That part of the claim is derived from reading migrate.go, not from a reproduced/executed result, so calling it 'confirmed' and 'reproducible' overstates what the log shows.
